falsifiable_hypothesis: Targetwise bounded cross-fit gains are noisy, but the 24-dimensional gain-shift vector provides a second-level signal detection problem. A positive-part James-Stein reliability greater than zero means the gain-shift vector has aggregate signal beyond its jackknife noise estimate. In that case the bounded raw gain vector is used. If the positive-part reliability is exactly zero, the previous verified amplitude-jackknife/unanimous-sign fallback is used unchanged.
gain_rule: Compute patient-count-weighted amplitude theta, prior gain g0_j, bounded raw gain graw_j in [1,3], K=3 bounded jackknife variance v_j, target reliability r_j, held-fold local gains, and the unanimous-sign fallback exactly as in unanimous_sign_boosted_gain. Let delta_j=graw_j-g0_j and R_global=max(0,1-(24-2)*mean_j(v_j)/sum_j(delta_j^2)), using R_global=0 when the denominator is numerically zero. If R_global>0, set all final gains to graw_j. Otherwise use the unanimous_sign_boosted_gain fallback gain. Apply qA=qA_loo_bagged and qB=qB_interpolated_jackknife-0.5*g_j*theta_j.
switch_rule: The only switch is the positive-part James-Stein boundary R_global>0, with no tuned threshold. The switch is computed independently inside each outer-training partition using fitting-only inner OOF statistics.

task_contract.ab_rule: average losses across separately costed A/B orientations; never average predictions
